sense.text:
The goal is to wake our people up, to snap them out of that wicked doctrine, Catholicism and Christianity, which is rampant in the northern kingdom countries and even in Africa, where there is more of the image of Caesar Borgia than anywhere.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: the Bible was written for us in this time, to learn who we are and what we must do to get out of this wicked system called Babylon.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We need a lot of patience and a lot of comfort, because we are going through trials and tribulations. We do not yet see the endgame: our salvation, the unity of Simeon and Levi. It is there, but we have to keep pushing and keep doing what the Most High ordained us to do, which is to prophesy and teach. And it is the scriptures first and foremost, always the scriptures. That is where the hope comes from.

The image hanging on the wall of the radio station in the Dominican Republic, the white Jesus, is Caesar Borgia. The book In the Pillory shows it plainly: a bust of the Saviour, posed for by Caesar Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander, and it was an open secret. It is a secret only to us, because we were taught not to read and not to write; Esau knows it. A man, an Edomite, posing as the Saviour.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.” The wicked is first and foremost Esau. He is the one setting up his doctrine, his propaganda and his images all through Africa, Europe and Latin America.

“He covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” That is exactly what the bust of the Saviour posed for by Caesar Borgia is: the wicked covered the faces of the judges with Caesar Borgia. That is the iconography of the Jesuit priests. Their picture of God and Adam, with a broken wrist and a finger reaching out, his little wiener out, and little naked boys going around, is demonic pedophile stuff. It is not righteous at all; you are supposed to have clothes on. We have to be wise to see it.

“Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.” The last days are from the time of Christ until now. Jacob was up in age, and he gathered his twelve sons to tell them what would come upon the twelve tribes of Israel in the last days.

“Simeon and Levi”: Simeon are the so-called Dominicans, and Levi are the so-called Haitians. They “are brethren.” Jacob had to remind them in the last days that they are brothers, because in the last days they would not be getting along. It is like two brothers fighting, and the father or mother says, stop, you are brothers, you are not supposed to behave like that. That is the goal of every mission to the island: to remind Simeon and Levi that they are brethren. Propaganda and revisionist history, pushed by the government, the news and the powers that be, keep them divided, while on the island itself the people say there is no conflict; they live side by side and marry one another.

“Instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.” The instruments of cruelty are the witchcraft on the island: voodoo. Levi is known for voodoo, but Simeon does it too. They call it 21 Divisions, a branch of voodoo from the Dominican Republic, but it is the same thing: the dancing, the rituals, the chants, the drums, the drinking, calling up evil, demonic spirits. Both call themselves Catholic and Christian, and on the side they go to the santero and the botanica, the witchcraft shop, and fill their houses with statues, cigars, coffee, beads and money to worship demonic entities. One of those statues is the so-called archangel Michael with his foot on the neck of a black demon, when the angels are black, God is black and Christ is black. That is how they twist the minds of Simeon to hate Levi, and to hate ourselves. This is why there is so much evil, death, destruction and earthquakes on the island of Hispaniola.

The sword is an instrument of cruelty too. We have to stop turning that machete, that sword, on our own people, and turn the sword spiritually on Esau, with the word of God.

“O my soul, come not thou into their secret”: Jacob is warning the other tribes not to get involved with Simeon and Levi in their witchcraft. A lot of the other tribes go to Haiti, and to the Dominican Republic, for magic, voodoo and spells, to get rich, to get a woman, to get a job.

“Unto their assembly, mine honour, be not thou united”: their assembly is when they come together in witchcraft and voodoo. The division you see on the island is of the Lord, because of the evil Simeon and Levi brought to Israel with their anger and with their witchcraft. Do not be united in that evil. The only way they will unite is with the word of God, under the black Messiah: not Caesar Borgia, not a white god, not Catholicism.

“For in their anger they slew a man”: that history is in Genesis 34, when Simeon and Levi put the man of Ham to death for dealing with their sister unrighteously, because we are not to mingle, mix or marry with the other nations.

“Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel.” Simeon and Levi are known for their quick and bad tempers. They are quick to fight, quick to pull out a machete, quick to cut, and they have no mercy. It is all over social media: Levi on Levi, Simeon on Simeon, Simeon against Levi. Their anger is a curse from the Most High for the evil they did.

“I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.” The tribe of Levi is divided among the twelve tribes and scattered to the four corners of the earth. Wherever you go, Latin America, Africa, Europe, you find Levi: Haitian communities in New York, Chicago, LA and Miami, in Europe, in Chile, Guatemala, Ecuador and Panama. It is prophecy.

precepts.why:
“There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination”: divination is witchcraft and magic; the voodoo priestess herself called them magicians. “An observer of times” reads tarot cards and worships the sun, moon and stars. “An enchanter” is the dancing and chanting you see at their ceremonies. “Or a witch”: a 21 Divisions witch, a voodoo priest. That is what the scripture is talking about.

“Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits”: the espiritista people go to consult. What should I do? I need a job, I need that woman, I need more money. Or, let me speak to my grandmother who passed away, she used to give me good guidance. “Or a wizard”, a magician like the priestess on the screen, “or a necromancer”, dealing with the dead: bones and skulls of real people, stolen from the cemeteries for rituals and kept in their houses.

“For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord.” Our people think it is good and righteous. It is a wicked, sinful act, and it is not of the Lord. “And because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.” So we have to speak out against these things, so that Simeon and Levi stop doing them. Some ninety percent of Levi practise voodoo, and Simeon does the same. That is why there is so much evil, death, destruction, earthquakes and trauma on the island of Hispaniola.

“A man also or woman that hath a familiar spirit”: a familiar spirit means a demon is on you. That is what they do; they conjure up demons, and you see them with their eyes rolled back, dancing, chanting and speaking in tongues. Those are demonic spirits.

“Or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death.” That was the punishment for witchcraft: brujería, santería, 21 Divisions, whatever name you give it. The names may not mean anything, but we know it is evil and it is of Satan.

“Many of them also which used curious arts”, strange rites, “brought their books together, and burned them before all men.” They have demonic books of incantations to conjure up demons.

That is what we must do. Once you learn this truth, once you know you are an Israelite of the tribe of Simeon, the tribe of Levi or any of the twelve tribes, and you are into this madness, you have to burn those books and destroy those statues, because they bring demons and evil into your house.

“And they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.” Those things are expensive. In the botanicas the statues are five feet tall, and our people pay top dollar for the candles, the prayers, the holy water and the books to interpret dreams. Break them and destroy them anyway.

“The graven images of their gods”: idols, the gods of the other nations. That is what our people are into, and we learned it from them, from Ham and from Esau, gods which are yet no gods. “Shall ye burn with fire.” Burn them, destroy them; they mean you no good and they can do no good.

“Thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee”: do not put it on you. If you have a gold chain with a cross that you paid a lot of money for, melt it down and turn it into something else, a menorah or an ephod, but do not wear it and do not keep it in your house. “Lest thou be snared therein”, caught in a trap. “For it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” The Most High God does not honour Caesar Borgia wrapped around your neck. That does not represent Christ; it represents the image of a man, Caesar Borgia, as we read in In the Pillory. Do not have no man, no white man, red man, Edomite man, on your neck.

“Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” We must do God’s commandments, not witchcraft, not 21 Divisions, not voodoo. We will not get through the gates of the kingdom, the city of God, through Christianity, Catholicism, witchcraft or voodoo.

“For without are dogs.” Dominican means dogs of the Lord. The history of the Inquisition shows it: the Dominicans in charge earned their title, dogs of the Lord, by ferreting out errors in the most hidden places and tearing their victims to bits. That was during the Spanish Inquisition in the 1400s, when they were kicking us out of Spain and Portugal and putting us to death if we would not convert, at the same time Columbus came to the Americas. They tore our children in half, hung our women with their babies, baptised the dead babies and fed them to the dogs. The real Dominicans are those priests, the dogs of the Lord, dogs of Satan really, and they put that name on the eastern side of the island to divide us from our brothers, the tribe of Levi. If you identify as a Dominican, or as a Haitian, you are not going to get the kingdom. There are twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel, and we must call ourselves what God called us: Simeon and Levi.

“And sorcerers”: the witches, the demonic enchanters. “And whoremongers”: a lot of those rituals are sex rituals, with adultery and fornication. “And murderers, and idolaters”, worshipping a white image of the Virgin Mary with a white baby Jesus. “And whosoever loveth and maketh a lie”: when you make those images, wear them and practise that witchcraft and idolatry, you are making a lie and continuing in the evil.

These are the names to have pride in: what the Most High called us, not what Esau labelled us. Dominican and Haitian are names of our captivity, not names God ordained.

“What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.” “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God.” The Bible defines itself. Israel is a prince that has power with God. Compare that with Dominican, dogs of the Lord. Who wants to be called a dog of the Lord? Yet our people on the island have pride in that name, anything to set themselves apart from their brothers the Haitians, because Haiti is kept at the bottom by design and by propaganda.

But the so-called Dominicans are in poverty too, whether they see it or not. Nothing on that island is run by them; it is run by white elites, Arabs, Japanese and Chinese, all the heathen, and we are the servants of our enemies.

Still on the witchcraft on the island of Simeon and Levi. “Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel.” No witchcraft can go against us if we keep God’s commandments. It cannot hurt us.

But if you believe in that stuff, if you are not keeping the commandments and you identify as a Haitian or a Dominican, it will affect you. You will be out of your mind, walking around talking to yourself. On the border, a Levi sister carrying a baby goat declared that it was a person. That is what witchcraft does to our people: you believe a goat is a person, or that your grandmother can turn into a wheelbarrow.

“According to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!” Witchcraft does not work on us when we are keeping God’s commandments.

sense.text:
Carnival is not a Dominican, Haitian, Brazilian or Israelite custom. Its roots go back to the pagan festivals of the Romans, the Saturnalia and Lupercalia, and the Greek Dionysian festivals of revelry and feasting; the word comes from carne levare, farewell to meat, before the Catholic season of Lent. It is masked balls, street parades, elaborate costumes, devil masks and loud music, and indulgence, meaning fornication and adultery, gotten out before they quote unquote repent for forty days of Lent and walk around with ashes on their foreheads thinking they are righteous. A dude in a fishnet shirt, belly out, licking a lollipop: that is some gay ass stuff. It is a temporary reversal of social rules: marriage, honouring and loving one another turned upside down. That day you can be a homo, like that fat homo with a lollipop in his mouth, and the women are butt ass naked shaking their ass. It is all demonic, idolatry and fornication, and for without are dogs: those practising it are not going to get the kingdom. The Romans and the Greeks gave it to us.

“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days”: an Israelite man was not allowed to keep the day the Most High made holy, nor the ancient feasts of Israel in captivity, “or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” That is why we call ourselves Dominican, Haitian, Latino and black: it was not lawful to call yourself a Jew.

“They were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices”: bitter constraint means forced, forced to eat swine’s flesh. “When the fast of Bacchus was kept”: Bacchanal and carnival are the same thing, feasting, revelry and excess. Bacchus was an idol, a false god of the Greeks and the Romans. “The Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus”, to march and parade, “carrying ivy.” That is why our people are dressed up carrying ivy and flowers; we saw it in Guatemala and Chile, carrying flowers for the Virgin Mary in costumes like the carnival ones.

Now we know where we got it: Esau forced it on us. It is not an Israelite custom. You will not find in Leviticus 23 that we must wear demonic masks, dance naked and give up all the laws, statutes and commandments.

“Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee”, the Greek ruler who ruled Egypt, “against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions.” We were not keeping it, so he made a law that we must. The same thing will happen in these last days: they will make laws that we must keep the Catholic religion, or whatever religion they come up with, and they will imprison and kill many of us. Right now our people follow these customs willingly, because we do not know our history and think we came up with them.

“And be partakers of their sacrifices.” They were sacrificing children, and it still happens. What comes out of carnival is carnival babies, conceived in those wicked parades, and because the child is not the husband’s, there is an abortion: children sacrificed unto these devils.

“And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death.” We were put to death. It is easy to say I would rather die, but a time is coming when you will have to choose God’s side or give up just to live a little longer in this wicked captivity. Better to die keeping God’s laws, as our forefathers did, because after this life we live on if we keep God’s commandments.

“Then might a man have seen the present misery.” That is the present misery of our people. They are not happy doing these things; it is slave trauma. The so-called Dominicans at carnival oil themselves with black, wear crosses, the religion of Caesar Borgia, and lick fire, the same as Trinidad and Brazil. Carnival was first practised in the Americas in La Vega and Santo Domingo in the early 1500s, right after Columbus, brought by the Spanish conquistadors through the Roman Catholic authorities, who put crosses on it to give it a semblance of righteousness. It began with the people dressing themselves as Moors and Christians: they were mocking the Israelites, the Moors, the morenos, who were expelled from Spain and Portugal in the 1400s.

Carnival is not a custom of the Israelites; we lost our customs. “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage.” We lost our heritage, and now we follow the customs forced on us from the time of the Greeks and the Romans until this present day. We have to stop following these wicked customs.

The carnival mocked the Moors, and the Moors were us. In 711 the Muslims conquered Spain together with the Jews, and the first to set foot on the soil of Spain was General Tarik, a Jew of the tribe of Simeon, after whom Tarifa is named. So the tribe of Simeon was the first to conquer Spain as the Moors, and when you see carnival, they are mocking that conquest and our expulsion.

The Jews, according to the prophecy, always dwelt alone, without intermixing with the nations, all descended from brown ancestors: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob must have been very dark, if not darker. The Spanish Jew always had a dark complexion and black hair. Now Simeon has to be reminded that he is black; he says he is not black, until ICE comes. White is right, improve the race, skin whitening, perming and blowing out the hair: that is the heritage we discontinued.

“This is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel”: Moses, the Levite man of God. A lot of brothers and sisters hate on the so-called Haitians, but if Moses were alive today they would call him a Haitian. He is of the tribe of Levi.

“From his right hand went a fiery law for them.” Moses gave us the laws, a fiery law we must keep to this day in order to come out of her, my people, and be not partakers of Babylon’s sins. Those laws have to burn within our spirit. They forced us to keep their wicked customs; we have to keep these laws willingly. That is key to our salvation.
“Yea, he loved the people.” Moses loved the people. “every one shall receive of thy words”: we have to receive the words of this book, do them and meditate upon them.

“Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.” This is our inheritance: not carnival, not brujería, not 21 Divisions, not santería, but the law. This Bible that the Most High blessed us to preserve for this day is our inheritance. “And he was king in Jeshurun”: Moses was king in Israel.

“And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one.” The Levites communicated with the Most High with the Urim and Thummim, not with witchcraft and enchantments. That was Levi on the righteous side. Now the so-called Haitians are on the side of wickedness, and we have to raise them up and teach them so they come out of it and get back to being the priests of the Most High, the lawgivers.

“Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands: smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again.” The so-called white man hates Levi. And Simeon, the so-called Dominicans, have to stop that hate, stop following their slave masters and the propaganda taught about their brother. Our neighbour is Levi. We are on the same island for a reason: to learn who we are, to get along, to end the division, and to be united in the faith of Christ.

They made a movie of Napoleon the conqueror and never showed his defeat at the hands of Levi. Toussaint Louverture, who abolished slavery on the whole island, was tricked into a meeting, imprisoned in France and kept alive for the war chest Napoleon believed he had hidden, but his army of freed black men defeated the French. Our people need that imagery: the mighty works of the tribe of Levi, rising up against our enemies the heathen. We need more Toussaint Louvertures and Jean-Jacques Dessalines.

Toussaint Louverture still believed in the French Republic, and that was his downfall. He was tricked into a meeting with the French general. In his proclamation of 1801 he said he made war with courage, honour and loyalty and received as brothers those who had fought under enemy flags; he wanted to make even the most ardent enemies of liberty love it. He was trying to convert Esau into loving him.

“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” His wickedness never goes away; there is no righteousness in Esau. That is what our people need to learn. We have to stop trying to assimilate and be equal. We are not equal to the so-called white man; the Most High says we are above all people that are upon the face of the earth. We have to change our mindset and teach it to our children when they wake up and when we walk in the streets.

The French did the same with slavery: forced to abolish it in 1793 and 1794, they violently brought it back under Napoleon. That is how Esau always does. Never trust thine enemy.

precepts.why:
This is why we bring these examples out: our people keep trying to convert and change the enemy, thinking there are good ones, good heathen out there. The scripture says never trust thine enemy.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Esau is the biblical name of the so-called white man. It is not personal, it is biblical: just as our biblical name is Israel, theirs is Esau, the profane person.

sense.text:
Toussaint Louverture told his officers that rank is the reward for honour, bravery and irreproachable conduct; that the higher they stood, the more irreproachable they must be, because the scandals of public men do more harm to society; that rank is not for ambition but for the general good; that every captain should have the best disciplined, cleanest and best trained company. That is the same thing expected of the brothers in God’s army: clean, disciplined, trained in the scriptures, bringing no shame on the purple and gold. We are not spicks, we are not Dominicans and Haitians, not rappers, not gangsters, not Bloods, not Crips. We are the twelve tribes of the nation of Israel. We come from royalty, from honour and respect, and we are bringing the government of Christ back on this earth: the Sabbath and the feast days are government, order, structure and heritage. And he laid out the obligation of fathers and mothers to raise their children in the love and fear of God.

This is similar. “Honour all men. Love the brotherhood.” Simeon and Levi are brethren; love the brotherhood. “Fear God. Honour the king”: honour Christ. That is what Toussaint Louverture, of the mighty tribe of Levi, was trying to express as best he could with Esau’s religion. Now we have the laws, the statutes, the commandments and the Most High’s word. It is our obligation as parents to teach our children, to govern ourselves and our people, and to stop following the wicked customs of the heathen.

Toussaint Louverture saw parents raising children in idleness, contempt for agriculture, rags and nudity, children who grow up without moral principles or a skill and become vagabonds, thieves and prostitutes. We see it on the island now, where tourists come for our young men and women. That is why we teach our children a skill and a trade, and why we must learn agriculture, because famine is coming. It is easier to raise strong children than to fix broken men.

This is Toussaint Louverture in the scriptures; he descends from the Maccabees. “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” Do not depend on Esau to do it, do not wait on welfare or handouts. Nobody is going to do it for us. It is within us, through the word and the spirit of the Most High, and it starts with each one of us. Toussaint knew it, the Maccabees knew it, and we have to know it.

Gregorio Luperón, a black general of the Dominican Restoration War, was born in Puerto Plata when it was part of Haiti. Ulises Heureaux, called Lilís, a black man and president of the Dominican Republic, was born in Puerto Plata too, and his father was born in Cap-Haïtien. A Dominican president of the tribe of Levi. Simeon and Levi share an intermingled, connected, rich history, and that is what will bring the two tribes together.

“The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together”: the northern kingdom and Judah were enslaved and held captive together, and together we will come out of it, as we did in the 1500s and the 1800s. Simeon and Levi are brethren.

“And all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.” Levi did not take Simeon captive; that is revisionist history. Haiti abolished slavery on the eastern side twice, in 1801 under Toussaint Louverture and in 1822 under Boyer, uniting the island; you cannot enslave a people and abolish slavery at the same time. What they did was remove the white elite, because they were the reason we were held captive. Haiti went on to help Bolívar on condition that he abolish slavery, and inspired revolts across the Americas. The Dominican independence day celebrates freedom from twenty-two years with Haiti instead of from Spain, which enslaved us for hundreds of years. In the Restoration War the black Dominican rebels called on Haiti to help throw off Spain, writing that we all live on the island of Haiti. Hispaniola received the first enslaved Africans in the Western Hemisphere in 1502, the first enslaved Israelites: the island is the cradle of blackness. Simeon has to love his blackness, because separating from Levi is separating from his brothers. Identify first as black and then as the Israelite; no matter how light-skinned you are, we are still black. Haiti occupied the eastern side for twenty-two years for the purpose of abolishing slavery, protecting against recolonization and erasing European power from the island. They held us fast; we had to fight for our freedom. Now we must keep the commandments and the faith of Christ for our freedom.

What unifies a people is a shared identity, a common history, common beliefs and a common enemy. Simeon and Levi are brethren; we are the nation of Israel. The law, the statutes, the commandments and the high holy days will unify them, and the common enemy is Esau. From the first, Simeon and Levi fought the common enemy together: they ran away to the mountains, and on Christmas Day 1522 the African and Indian slaves on Diego Columbus’s plantation rose and killed their masters, to kill Esau, because he enslaved, tortured, raped and robbed us. So the Europeans concluded they must use one race to fight the other, and that between the races they could not dig too deep a gulf. That is the Willie Lynch division: different names, languages and shades to keep us apart. It is the same today. Neo-Nazis in the Dominican Republic work with the government to prevent solidarity with the Haitian people. ICE shot a Simeon brother in the Bronx, and the Dominican authorities killed a Levi brother who looks just like him: black people killing black people, coons amongst us, because we do not know who our brother is or who the real enemy is. If you are angry about the brother in the Bronx, you have to be angry about the Levi brothers killed by their own brother.

“He delivereth the poor in his affliction.” Levi repents quickly, whole families, because Levi is afflicted with so much oppression. Simeon is comfortable under Esau, the so-called white man, and needs to feel it. It sounds unfortunate, but more shootings and more killings have to happen for Simeon to wake up.

“And openeth their ears in oppression.” In his sorrow, pain and anguish, then he is ready to listen: that he is of the tribe of Simeon and the so-called Haitians are his brothers. Oppression is when we listen; that is when we are ready for repentance.

“Gather yourselves together”: that is what our forefather Jacob said to his sons. “Yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” The other nations do not desire us. No matter how much we try to fit in and assimilate, they do not desire us.

“Before the decree bring forth”: before the destruction comes, “before the day pass”, before Christ returns and turns this place to rubble. He does not want to find you in witchcraft, brujería, santería or 21 Divisions. Repent as Israelites and come together as the tribe of Simeon and the tribe of Levi, so that we grow as the nation of Israel, keeping God’s commandments with honour, respect and dignity. That is our obligation and our duty.
